title: DA envelope capture fails for EVERY async/background mb3-critic dispatch (missing_envelope)
observation: All mb3-critic dispatches of the session (TASK-015 x2, TASK-016 x3 confirmed in tasks-registry.jsonl; TASK-017 x4 by the same pattern) ended as da_extraction_failed reason=missing_envelope, has_schema_envelope=false, invocation_mode=manual_advisory — even when the critic output ended with a correctly fenced mb3-critic.review/v2 JSON envelope as the absolute final element. Correlated: repeated da_dispatcher_decision {source: subagent-stop, decision: ignore, reason: not_declared} every ~20s around each dispatch. Zero da_reviewed events persisted all session; iteration counts could not anchor to the event log.
dst_frame: D4 DA-capture write-surface: the subagent-stop capture path does not recognize ASYNC Agent dispatches whose final text arrives via task-notification rather than an inline tool result. Sim vector: dispatch-declared vs undeclared subagent-stop event -> capture decision.
mb3_proposal: Support envelope extraction at subagent-stop for async/background agents (declare the dispatch so the dispatcher does not ignore as not_declared), or document that critics MUST be dispatched synchronously for capture. Filed as REQ-002.

title: semantic-upsert path: no OCC fields + mode=replace COMPACTS per-section event history
observation: Events written via mb3_artifact upsert_section carry no event_id/base_revision/base_hash (unlike OCC-guarded evidence_added AEV-* events). mode=replace physically destroys the prior event for the section (last-write-wins): a flawed 11:58:16Z event carrying an auto-captured dangling ur_ref vanished from artifact-events/implementation.jsonl after replacement — no supersession pointer, no recoverable history. This misled a remediation narrative (claimed event-sourcing supersession) until a DA pass caught the claim as unverifiable against the log.

health_signal.capture: event_store_revision matches post-compaction log; original event unrecoverable

dst_frame: D2 event-store append surface: invariant "journal is append-only; replacement is supersession-with-audit" VIOLATED by design or by bug. Sim vector: two writers upsert the same section concurrently -> silent clobber, no conflict detection.
mb3_proposal: Align semantic-upsert with event_id/OCC discipline + append-with-supersession, or document compaction+no-OCC as intentional. Filed as REQ-003.

title: repro: async mb3-critic dispatch -> da_extraction_failed(missing_envelope)
op_sequence: 1) mb3_task start (any task, IMPLEMENT); 2) Agent(subagent_type=mb3-critic) dispatched ASYNC/background; 3) critic returns text ending with fenced ```mb3-critic.review/v2 JSON envelope via task-notification; 4) subagent-stop fires -> da_dispatcher_decision {decision: ignore, reason: not_declared}; 5) claude-hook writes da_extraction_failed {reason: missing_envelope, has_schema_envelope: false, invocation_mode: manual_advisory}
invariant: a well-formed mb3-critic.review/v2 envelope in the critic FINAL output is captured as exactly one da_reviewed event for the (task, phase) pair
fault: dispatch-mode blindness: async final text arrives via task-notification, not inline tool result; dispatcher treats subagent-stop as not_declared and hook sees no envelope surface
observation: 100% reproduction across >=5 confirmed dispatches (2 tasks, 2 phases-worth of gates); zero da_reviewed persisted all session

title: repro: upsert_section mode=replace destroys prior section event (no supersession)
op_sequence: 1) mb3_artifact upsert_section {section: S, content: C1 containing a bare UR-token} -> event E1 appended with auto-captured ur_refs; 2) mb3_artifact upsert_section {section: S, mode: replace, content: C2} -> E1 REMOVED from artifact-events/<name>.jsonl, only E2 remains; 3) materialize -> projection consistent with compacted log; 4) grep for the UR-token across the task dir -> 0 matches (history unrecoverable)
invariant: artifact event journal is append-only; a replace is a superseding event preserving the audit trail
fault: replace-mode compaction (last-write-wins per section) + no event_id/base_revision/base_hash on the semantic-upsert path -> concurrent same-section writers silently clobber; audit narratives cannot distinguish superseded from destroyed
seam: semantic-upsert write path <-> OCC-guarded evidence_added write path (dual-path inconsistency)
observation: observed live in TASK-017: the 11:58:16Z flawed event vanished after replacement; event count and event_store_revision stayed consistent so nothing flagged the destruction

title: ur_refs auto-capture scans section BODY TEXT for UR-tokens -> dangling cross-namespace refs
observation: upsert_section auto-scanned prose mentioning the PRD-scoped identifier (a bare UR-007 token in a sentence about PRD.md history) and stamped it into the event ur_refs, creating a citation to a task-level UR that never existed (task URs stopped at UR-003). Caught by DA as F-IMPL-VERIFY2-2; only fixable by rewriting the text to avoid the bare token (which, combined with replace-compaction, destroyed the flawed event).
dst_frame: D2/D7: ur_refs should come from an explicit parameter (like evidence urRefs), not implicit body-text scanning; invariant: every ur_ref resolves to an existing UR in the SAME task namespace.
mb3_proposal: Validate auto-captured ur_refs against the task requests registry and drop/flag non-resolving tokens; or capture only from an explicit urRefs param.

title: materialize discards pre-event direct-markdown writes + duplicates headers when content embeds them
observation: (1) A first upsert_section write that landed as sourceKind=markdown directly in implementation.md was silently DISCARDED when materialize later rebuilt the file from the event store (sections went empty). (2) When section content includes its own "## <name>" header line, materialize emits the header twice (template header + in-content header). Neither behavior is documented at the tool surface; both were caught by DA passes, took 3 rewrite rounds to converge.
dst_frame: D2 projection determinism: materialize(events) must be total over BOTH write paths or the markdown path must be rejected loudly; header supply contract (materializer owns headers) is implicit.
mb3_proposal: Either event-source the direct-markdown path too, or make materialize refuse/warn when a non-evented write would be discarded; document that section content must NOT embed its own header.

title: evidence/evidence_batch parameter discovery is trial-and-error; one shape crashes with a raw TypeError
observation: Guessing the evidence record shape produced: {items:[...]} -> refused empty_batch (wrong key, no hint that the key is records); {ur,phase,evidence} -> refused empty_content; adding content -> refused missing_artifact; adding artifact -> CRASH "undefined is not an object (evaluating s.trim)" (missing section, unguarded). Correct shape ({artifact,section,content,urRefs}) had to be reverse-engineered from mb3-core CLI source. Also: mb3_issue annotate works only for ISS ids — a REQ cannot be annotated at all (error: issue REQ-002 not found), so a factual correction had to live in a task artifact instead.
dst_frame: §0: read/validation surface -> DST silent; pure ergonomics.
mb3_proposal: Refusals should name the expected keys (records[], artifact/section/content) and the s.trim crash needs a guard; give REQ/FT records an annotate path or route annotate to them.

title: mb3 CLI absent in PATH while CLAUDE.md instructs CLI-first (mb3 create ...)
observation: Managed CLAUDE.md sections instruct commands like mb3 create / mb3 model-routing plan, but the shell has no mb3 binary (command not found); all operations had to go through MCP tools. Minor, but every fresh session pays the discovery cost.
mb3_proposal: Either ship/alias the mb3 CLI into PATH during project init, or make the managed CLAUDE.md text point at the MCP tool names as the primary surface.

frictions: Top: (1) DA envelope capture failed for 100% of async critic dispatches (REQ-002) — the DA loop ran fully advisory all session; (2) semantic-upsert store path: no OCC + replace compacts history (REQ-003); (3) ur_refs auto-capture from body text made a dangling cross-namespace ref; (4) materialize discards non-evented markdown writes and duplicates embedded headers — 3 rewrite rounds to converge; (5) evidence/* param shapes undiscoverable, one unguarded TypeError.
wrong_routes: Tried CLI mb3 (absent) before MCP; tried annotate on a REQ (ISS-only); guessed evidence_batch key items instead of records; wrote first artifact content as direct markdown (later discarded by materialize).
ergonomics: MCP actions are strong once shapes are known, but refusal messages rarely name the expected keys; dual write paths (evidence vs semantic-upsert vs direct markdown) with different guarantees is the main conceptual trap.
feedback_quality: DA critic quality was excellent — every REVISE round found real, verifiable defects (incl. in my own remediation narrative). Refusal/error surfaces are the weak spot.
overhead: 4 DA rounds on TASK-017 for what was a 6-line config change — most of the overhead came from artifact-store mechanics (materialize/headers/ur_refs), not from the code change itself.
wishlist: (a) capture async critic envelopes (REQ-002); (b) OCC + supersession on semantic-upsert (REQ-003); (c) validate auto ur_refs; (d) materialize should reject or event-source direct markdown writes; (e) refusals name expected keys; (f) annotate for REQ/FT.
dst_log_dogfood: Enabled at session end retroactively; capture from fresh memory + persisted registries was straightforward; append/status UX fine.
transport: MCP daemon stable all session; no -32001; the only transport-class failure was one subagent killed by the account session limit (resumed via SendMessage successfully).
what_worked_well: mb3_task render syncing UR checklists; the ARCH.md Edit-block hook correctly forcing the managed write path; task lifecycle (create/start/close_check/close) friction-free; the ISS-2596-guarded dst-log script itself.
repro_candidates: Both op records: async-critic capture miss (deterministic, 5/5) and replace-compaction clobber (deterministic; concurrency variant needs a 2-writer sim).
